**The Meaning of the Verses:**

Allah the Exalted says, ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture and the polytheists﴾. After clarifying the true religion that saves from punishment and brings about bliss, which is the Islamic religion, Allah the Exalted informs us that whoever among the People of the Scripture and the polytheists rejects it will be in the fire of Hell, abiding therein forever. This is Allah's ruling concerning them, because of their disbelief in the truth, their turning away from it after the clear proof had come to them, and their knowing the way yet deviating from it. They were content with falsehood and satisfied with disbelief and polytheism instead of faith and monotheism. These disbelieving, wicked people are the worst of all creation. This is the meaning of His words, ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture and the polytheists will be in the fire of Hell, abiding therein forever. They are the worst of creation﴾.

Allah the Exalted also informs us that the reward of those who believe in Allah and His Messenger and act according to the Islamic religion, fulfilling the obligatory duties (fara'id) and avoiding the prohibitions (nawahi), and who hasten to good deeds and righteous acts, is that they are the best of creation. He says, ﴿Indeed, those who believed and did righteous deeds, those are the best of creation﴾. His words, ﴿Their reward with their Lord﴾, mean the reward of those who believed in Allah and His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) and in what he brought of guidance and the true religion. They are the best of creation. His words, ﴿Their reward with their Lord﴾, also mean the day they meet Him, which is after death. ﴿Gardens of perpetual residence﴾ means gardens of lasting abode, ﴿abiding therein forever﴾, meaning they will never leave them nor die, ever.

His words, ﴿Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him﴾, mean that Allah is pleased with them because of their faith and obedience, and they are pleased with Him because of what He has granted and bestowed upon them of enduring bliss in the Abode of Peace.

His words, the Exalted, ﴿That is for whoever fears his Lord﴾, mean that this mentioned reward is a great reward, in which its people are granted both the happiness of the soul and the happiness of the body together. It is the reward of a servant who feared his Lord, so he did not disobey Him until he met Him after death. If he disobeyed Him one day, he repented, and if he erred, he returned, until he died while in obedience and not in disobedience.

**Guidance from the Verses:**

1. Explanation of the reward of whoever among all people rejects Islam, and that it is an evil reward.

2. Explanation of the reward of whoever believes in Islam, enters into it, applies its principles, and remains steadfast in its commands and prohibitions. It is an excellent reward: the pleasure of Allah and eternal life in the Abode of Peace.

3. The excellence of fear of Allah, when it leads its possessor to obey Allah and His Messenger, so that he obeys them by performing the obligatory duties and abstaining from what is forbidden, in belief, speech and action.

Allah the Exalted says, ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture and the polytheists﴾. After clarifying the true religion that saves from punishment and brings about bliss, which is the Islamic religion, Allah the Exalted informs us that whoever among the People of the Scripture and the polytheists rejects it will be in the fire of Hell, abiding therein forever. This is Allah's ruling concerning them, because of their disbelief in the truth, their turning away from it after the clear proof had come to them, and their knowing the way yet deviating from it. They were content with falsehood and satisfied with disbelief and polytheism instead of faith and monotheism. These disbelieving, wicked people are the worst of all creation. This is the meaning of His words, ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture and the polytheists will be in the fire of Hell, abiding therein forever. They are the worst of creation﴾.

Allah the Exalted also informs us that the reward of those who believe in Allah and His Messenger and act according to the Islamic religion, fulfilling the obligatory duties (fara'id) and avoiding the prohibitions (nawahi), and who hasten to good deeds and righteous acts, is that they are the best of creation. He says, ﴿Indeed, those who believed and did righteous deeds, those are the best of creation﴾. His words, ﴿Their reward with their Lord﴾, mean the reward of those who believed in Allah and His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) and in what he brought of guidance and the true religion. They are the best of creation. His words, ﴿Their reward with their Lord﴾, also mean the day they meet Him, which is after death. ﴿Gardens of perpetual residence﴾ means gardens of lasting abode, ﴿abiding therein forever﴾, meaning they will never leave them nor die, ever.

His words, ﴿Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him﴾, mean that Allah is pleased with them because of their faith and obedience, and they are pleased with Him because of what He has granted and bestowed upon them of enduring bliss in the Abode of Peace.

His words, the Exalted, ﴿That is for whoever fears his Lord﴾, mean that this mentioned reward is a great reward, in which its people are granted both the happiness of the soul and the happiness of the body together. It is the reward of a servant who feared his Lord, so he did not disobey Him until he met Him after death. If he disobeyed Him one day, he repented, and if he erred, he returned, until he died while in obedience and not in disobedience.

**Guidance from the Verses:**

1. Explanation of the reward of whoever among all people rejects Islam, and that it is an evil reward.

2. Explanation of the reward of whoever believes in Islam, enters into it, applies its principles, and remains steadfast in its commands and prohibitions. It is an excellent reward: the pleasure of Allah and eternal life in the Abode of Peace.

3. The excellence of fear of Allah, when it leads its possessor to obey Allah and His Messenger, so that he obeys them by performing the obligatory duties and abstaining from what is forbidden, in belief, speech and action.
